quests.sentence: She forgot her umbrella and got completely soaked in the rain.
quests.hint: 'Forgot' and 'got soaked' are both past tense - this has already happened.
quests.explanation: 'Forgot' and 'got soaked' are both simple past tense forms. The sentence describes a completed sequence of past events.

quests.sentence: She always checks the weather forecast before leaving the house in the morning.
quests.hint: 'Always' signals a consistent, unbroken present habit.
quests.explanation: 'Checks' is the present simple. 'Always' is a frequency adverb confirming this is a firm current habit.

quests.sentence: She is going to buy a reliable waterproof coat this weekend.
quests.hint: 'This weekend' is still to come, and 'is going to' signals a clear plan.
quests.explanation: 'Is going to buy' is the 'going to' future for a decided plan. 'This weekend' is a near-future time reference.

quests.sentence: The headteacher announced the new school uniform policy last term.
quests.hint: 'Last term' is a school period that has already ended.
quests.explanation: 'Announced' is the simple past. 'Last term' is a completed past time period.

quests.sentence: The headteacher announces any changes to school policies during assembly.
quests.hint: This describes how announcements normally happen - a general present procedure.
quests.explanation: 'Announces' is the present simple for a general procedure. It describes how things currently work at the school.

quests.sentence: The headteacher will announce the end-of-year exam results on Friday afternoon.
quests.hint: 'On Friday afternoon' is a future time that hasn't arrived yet.
quests.explanation: 'Will announce' is the future simple. 'On Friday afternoon' is a future time marker.

quests.sentence: The new manager introduced herself to the whole team on her very first day.
quests.hint: 'On her first day' is a specific past moment - that day has already happened.
quests.explanation: 'Introduced' is the simple past. 'On her first day' is a specific completed past event.

quests.sentence: The manager meets with each team member individually every month.
quests.hint: 'Every month' shows a regular, scheduled present routine.
quests.explanation: 'Meets' is the present simple. 'Every month' confirms this is an ongoing regular practice.

quests.sentence: The manager will hold the annual performance reviews at the end of next month.
quests.hint: 'End of next month' is a future time reference.
quests.explanation: 'Will hold' is the future simple. 'At the end of next month' is a clear future time marker.

quests.sentence: The chef was carefully preparing the desserts when the health inspector arrived.
quests.hint: 'Was preparing' describes an action in progress at a past moment.
quests.explanation: 'Was preparing' is the past continuous - an action in progress when another past event occurred. Both are in the past.

quests.sentence: The chef prepares all ingredients fresh every single morning before service begins.
quests.hint: 'Every morning' shows a regular daily routine.
quests.explanation: 'Prepares' is the present simple for a regular routine. 'Every morning' confirms this is an ongoing daily habit.

quests.sentence: The chef will prepare a special five-course tasting menu for the opening night.
quests.hint: This describes a planned event that hasn't taken place yet.
quests.explanation: 'Will prepare' is the future simple. The sentence describes a plan for a specific future occasion.

quests.sentence: The doctor prescribed a course of antibiotics for her chest infection.
quests.hint: 'Prescribed' is past tense - the doctor has already given the prescription.
quests.explanation: 'Prescribed' is the simple past. The sentence describes a completed medical consultation.

quests.sentence: The doctor prescribes antibiotics only when they are absolutely necessary.
quests.hint: This describes the doctor's general current practice - a policy statement.
quests.explanation: 'Prescribes' is the present simple, describing a general medical policy that applies now.

quests.sentence: The doctor is going to refer her to a specialist at the hospital next week.
quests.hint: 'Next week' is a future time, and 'is going to refer' signals a firm plan.
quests.explanation: 'Is going to refer' is the 'going to' future for a decided plan. 'Next week' confirms the referral is ahead.

quests.sentence: The last ferry left the island harbour at seven o'clock last evening.
quests.hint: 'Last evening' is a period of time that has already passed.
quests.explanation: 'Left' is the past tense of 'leave'. 'Last evening' is a completed past time reference.

quests.sentence: The ferry departs from the island harbour every evening at seven o'clock.
quests.hint: Timetabled events use the present simple - they describe a regular, ongoing schedule.
quests.explanation: 'Departs' is the present simple, used for regular timetables and schedules. The departure time is a current ongoing fact.

quests.sentence: The ferry will run on a reduced winter schedule from next November onwards.
quests.hint: 'From next November' is a future time point that hasn't arrived.
quests.explanation: 'Will run' is the future simple. 'From next November onwards' is a clear future time reference.

quests.sentence: By the time she arrived at the family party, all the food had been eaten.
quests.hint: 'Had been eaten' happened before her arrival - both events are in the past.
quests.explanation: 'Had been eaten' is the past perfect. Her arrival was also in the past, and the eating happened before that.

quests.sentence: By the time she arrives at family gatherings, the food is usually almost gone.
quests.hint: This describes what typically happens - a general present truth.
quests.explanation: 'Arrives' and 'is' are present simple verbs. The sentence describes a recurring present situation.

quests.sentence: By the time she arrives tomorrow evening, we will have saved a plate for her.
quests.hint: 'Tomorrow evening' is a future time, and 'will have saved' will be complete by then.
quests.explanation: 'Will have saved' is the future perfect - an action that will be done before a future point ('tomorrow evening').

quests.sentence: She had backed up all her important files before the hard drive completely failed.
quests.hint: 'Had backed up' happened before the failure - both events are in the past.
quests.explanation: 'Had backed up' is the past perfect. The backing up was completed before the hard drive failed, which is also past.

quests.sentence: She backs up her files to the cloud every Sunday without fail.
quests.hint: 'Every Sunday' signals a regular weekly habit.
quests.explanation: 'Backs up' is the present simple for a regular routine. 'Every Sunday without fail' confirms it is ongoing.

quests.sentence: She will back up her new laptop as soon as she finishes setting it up today.
quests.hint: 'As soon as she finishes setting it up today' refers to a future moment.
quests.explanation: 'Will back up' is the future simple. 'As soon as she finishes' is a future condition.

quests.sentence: He spent all his birthday money on a new pair of limited-edition trainers.
quests.hint: 'Spent' is past tense - the purchase has already been made.
quests.explanation: 'Spent' is the simple past of 'spend'. The sentence describes a completed past purchase.

quests.sentence: He saves a portion of his monthly wages to put towards larger purchases.
quests.hint: This describes a regular habit - what he does currently.

quests.sentence: He will buy the new gaming console when it goes on sale next month.
quests.hint: 'Next month' is a future time that hasn't arrived yet.

quests.sentence: She had read all three books in the series before the first film was released.
quests.hint: 'Had read' was completed before another past event - the film release.
quests.explanation: 'Had read' is the past perfect. The reading was done before another past event (the film release).

quests.sentence: She reads at least one novel every month to keep up with her book club.
quests.hint: 'Every month' signals a regular monthly habit.
quests.explanation: 'Reads' is the present simple for a regular habit. 'Every month' confirms this is an ongoing routine.

quests.sentence: She will read the new bestseller on the long-haul flight next week.
